text: In which year was the Football Association founded in London?
explanation: The FA was formed on 26 October 1863 at the Freemasons' Tavern in London and published the first Laws of the Game that December.

text: Which club, founded in 1857, is recognised by FIFA as the oldest football club still in existence?
explanation: Sheffield FC was founded in 1857, six years before the FA. Notts County (1862) is the oldest professional club.

text: Who won the first FA Cup final in 1872?
explanation: Wanderers beat Royal Engineers 1–0 at Kennington Oval on 16 March 1872.

text: The first official international match, played in 1872, was between which two teams?
explanation: Scotland and England drew 0–0 at Hamilton Crescent in Glasgow on 30 November 1872.

text: Which club won the first Football League title in 1888–89 without losing a match?
explanation: Preston North End, 'The Invincibles', went unbeaten in the league and also won the FA Cup without conceding a goal.

text: Which Aston Villa director founded the Football League in 1888?
explanation: William McGregor wrote to the leading clubs in 1888 proposing regular fixtures, which became the Football League.

text: In which year was the penalty kick added to the Laws of the Game?
explanation: The penalty kick, proposed by Irish goalkeeper William McCrum, was adopted by the International Football Association Board in 1891.

text: In which decade were goal nets, patented by Liverpool engineer John Brodie, introduced?
explanation: Brodie patented goal nets in 1890; they were trialled in 1891 and used in the FA Cup final in 1892.

text: In which city was FIFA founded in 1904?
explanation: FIFA was founded on 21 May 1904 at the headquarters of the French sports union in Paris. It moved to Zurich in 1932.

text: After the 1925 offside change, how many opponents did an attacker need between himself and the goal line?
explanation: The requirement dropped from three opponents to two in 1925, and goals per game rose sharply the next season.

text: Which country won the Olympic football tournaments of 1924 and 1928?
explanation: Uruguay won in Paris in 1924 and in Amsterdam in 1928, beating Argentina in the 1928 final after a replay.

text: What is the first FA Cup final at Wembley, in 1923, known as?
explanation: Huge crowds spilled onto the pitch and PC George Scorey on his grey horse Billie helped clear it. Bolton beat West Ham 2–0.

text: In 1921 the FA banned women's football from its members' grounds. In which year was the ban lifted?
explanation: The ban came after women's matches such as Dick, Kerr Ladies' Boxing Day 1920 game drew 53,000 at Goodison Park. It lasted 50 years.

text: Which country hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
explanation: Uruguay beat Argentina 4–2 in the final at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo.

author: tifosi_luca
text: Which nation won both the 1934 and 1938 World Cups?
explanation: Italy won at home in 1934 and retained the trophy in France in 1938.

text: Who coached Italy to both the 1934 and 1938 World Cup titles?
explanation: Vittorio Pozzo is still the only coach to win two World Cups.

text: Why were no World Cups held in 1942 and 1946?
wrong: A boycott by South American teams
explanation: The war cancelled both tournaments; the World Cup returned in Brazil in 1950.

text: Herbert Chapman's Arsenal popularised which formation after the 1925 offside change?
explanation: Chapman pulled the centre-half back into defence, creating the WM that dominated English football into the 1950s.

text: What is Uruguay's 2–1 win over Brazil at the Maracanã in the deciding match of the 1950 World Cup called?
explanation: Brazil needed only a draw in front of about 200,000 people, but goals from Schiaffino and Ghiggia won it for Uruguay.

text: Which team beat Hungary's 'Magical Magyars' in the 1954 World Cup final, the 'Miracle of Bern'?
explanation: West Germany came from 2–0 down to win 3–2, ending Hungary's unbeaten run of more than four years.

text: In 1953 Hungary became the first team from outside the British Isles to beat England at Wembley. What was the score?
explanation: Puskás, Hidegkuti and Kocsis took England apart; Hungary then won the return match 7–1 in Budapest.

text: Which club won the first five European Cups, from 1956 to 1960?
explanation: Led by Alfredo Di Stéfano, Real Madrid won the first five editions, finishing with a 7–3 win over Eintracht Frankfurt in Glasgow.

text: Aged 17, who became the youngest player to score in a World Cup final, in 1958?
explanation: Pelé scored twice in Brazil's 5–2 win over Sweden in Stockholm.

text: How many goals did Just Fontaine score at the 1958 World Cup, still the record for a single tournament?
explanation: France's Just Fontaine scored 13 goals in six matches in Sweden.

text: Who won the first Ballon d'Or, in 1956?
explanation: Blackpool's Stanley Matthews, then 41, won the first award from France Football. Di Stéfano was second.

text: Lev Yashin is the only goalkeeper to have won the Ballon d'Or. In which year did he win it?
explanation: The Dynamo Moscow keeper, the 'Black Spider', won it in 1963.

text: Who scored a hat-trick in the 1966 World Cup final?
explanation: Hurst's three goals helped England beat West Germany 4–2 after extra time at Wembley.

text: Which was the first British club to win the European Cup, in 1967?
explanation: Celtic's 'Lisbon Lions', all born within 30 miles of Celtic Park, beat Inter 2–1 in Lisbon.

text: Why did Brazil get to keep the Jules Rimet Trophy after the 1970 World Cup?
answer: It was their third World Cup title
wrong: They won every match without conceding
FIFA retired the trophy after the war
The final was played in Brazil
explanation: Under the original rules the first nation to win three times kept the trophy; Brazil won in 1958, 1962 and 1970.

text: At which World Cup were yellow and red cards first used?
explanation: Referee Ken Aston came up with the idea after confusion over cautions at the 1966 World Cup; cards debuted in Mexico in 1970.

author: samba_bia
text: Which coach is most associated with 'Total Football' at Ajax and the Netherlands?
explanation: Michels built the system at Ajax and took it to the 1974 World Cup final; Cruyff was its star on the pitch.

text: In which years did Ajax win three European Cups in a row?
explanation: Ajax beat Panathinaikos, Inter and Juventus in those three finals.

author: porteno_mateo
text: Which club won the European Cup three years running from 1974 to 1976?
explanation: Beckenbauer, Müller and Maier led Bayern past Atlético Madrid, Leeds United and Saint-Étienne.

author: kaiser_jonas
text: Against which country did Diego Maradona score the 'Hand of God' goal in 1986?
explanation: In the quarter-final in Mexico City Maradona scored with his hand, then dribbled past half the team for the 'Goal of the Century'. Argentina won 2–1.

text: Who won the first FIFA Women's World Cup, held in China in 1991?
explanation: The USA beat Norway 2–1 in the final in Guangzhou, with two goals from Michelle Akers.

text: Which 1992 law change stopped goalkeepers from picking up deliberate passes from teammates' feet?
explanation: After a defensive, time-wasting 1990 World Cup, the IFAB banned keepers from handling deliberate back-passes from 1992.

text: Which 1989 disaster led to the Taylor Report and all-seater stadiums in England's top divisions?
explanation: 97 Liverpool supporters died after a crush at Hillsborough in Sheffield. Lord Justice Taylor's report required all-seater grounds.

text: Arrigo Sacchi's AC Milan won back-to-back European Cups in which years?
explanation: Milan beat Steaua Bucharest 4–0 in 1989 and Benfica 1–0 in 1990, the last club to retain the trophy until Real Madrid in 2017.

text: Which season was the first of the English Premier League?
explanation: The top clubs broke away from the Football League to sell their own TV rights; Manchester United won the first title.

text: What did the 1995 Bosman ruling by the European Court of Justice allow?
answer: Out-of-contract players to move between EU clubs on a free transfer
wrong: Clubs to be owned by foreign investors
Players to represent two national teams
explanation: Belgian midfielder Jean-Marc Bosman won his case; the ruling also ended foreign-player quotas for EU nationals.

text: Which club won the Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League treble in 1999?
explanation: United scored twice in stoppage time to beat Bayern Munich 2–1 in the final in Barcelona.

text: Who scored the golden goal that won the Euro 2000 final for France against Italy?
explanation: Wiltord equalised in stoppage time and Trezeguet volleyed the winner in extra time in Rotterdam.

author: ultras_ana
text: Which tournament did Greece win as huge underdogs in 2004?
explanation: Otto Rehhagel's Greece beat hosts Portugal 1–0 in the final in Lisbon with a header from Angelos Charisteas.

text: From which club did Real Madrid sign Zinedine Zidane for a world-record fee in 2001?
explanation: The fee was about €77 million, a world record that stood until Real signed Cristiano Ronaldo in 2009.

author: culer_marta
text: Liverpool came back from 3–0 down at half-time to win the 2005 Champions League final against which club?
explanation: Liverpool scored three in six minutes in Istanbul and won the shoot-out after a 3–3 draw.

text: Who scored the winning goal in the 2010 World Cup final?
explanation: Iniesta scored in the 116th minute against the Netherlands in Johannesburg, giving Spain their first World Cup.

author: oranje_daan
text: In which calendar year did Pep Guardiola's Barcelona win six trophies out of six?
explanation: La Liga, Copa del Rey, Champions League, Spanish and European Super Cups and the Club World Cup, all in 2009.

text: Which team beat hosts Brazil 7–1 in the 2014 World Cup semi-final?
explanation: Germany led 5–0 after 29 minutes in Belo Horizonte and went on to win the final against Argentina.

text: Which country won the 2011 Women's World Cup, beating the USA on penalties in the final?
explanation: Japan twice came from behind to draw 2–2 in Frankfurt, then won the shoot-out 3–1.

author: kop_end_sam
text: Leicester City won the 2015–16 Premier League at pre-season bookmaker odds of about what?
explanation: Claudio Ranieri's side, nearly relegated the season before, won the title by ten points.

text: At which men's World Cup was VAR used for the first time?
explanation: The IFAB wrote VAR into the Laws in March 2018 and FIFA used it at every match in Russia.

text: Neymar's 2017 move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain set a world-record fee of about how much?
explanation: PSG paid Neymar's €222 million release clause, more than double the previous record.

text: Who won the 2022 World Cup final in Qatar on penalties after a 3–3 draw?
explanation: Messi scored twice and Mbappé hit a hat-trick before Argentina won the shoot-out 4–2 at the Lusail Stadium.

text: Which country won the 2023 Women's World Cup?
explanation: Spain beat England 1–0 in Sydney with a goal from captain Olga Carmona.

text: How many teams take part in the 2026 men's World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico?
explanation: FIFA expanded the tournament from 32 teams to 48 starting in 2026.

text: Which player has won the most Ballon d'Or awards, with eight?
explanation: Messi won in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021 and 2023. Ronaldo has five.

author: almaty_arman
text: Which tournament did England's women win at Wembley in 2022?
explanation: England beat Germany 2–1 after extra time in front of 87,192 people, a European Championship record.
